title: The agy-claude boot model check reads a structured source instead of the TUI footer
source: console, 2026-10-07 L2 landing (review convergence: rounds 5-7 found ~18 of 27 findings in the footer heuristic)
summary: L2's launch model check decides whether agy booted Claude by reading the label on agy's footer-prefix line (bridge/launch_model_verification.go, panestream.FooterModelLabel). A TUI footer can take endless shapes, so every adversarial review found a new one (rounds 5-7). Round 7 made every miss fail safe (unreadable gives 87, which fails over to Claude Code). Two limits remain: healthy footers that are split, use a bullet separator, or are NBSP-padded read as unreadable (needless failovers), and a Gemini boot verifies as Claude only if agy draws a footer-prefix line whose own label names Claude.
fix: Read the booted model from a structured source: the existing modelquery /model capture after boot, or agy's own state or settings if they record the active model. Keep the footer read only as a fallback signal. One home for the family decision (modelquery.FamiliesIn).
acceptance: The model check decides from a structured source on a real agy-claude boot (characterized against a captured /model response or agy state, red first)
A split, bullet-separated or NBSP-padded healthy footer no longer causes a failover
A Gemini boot is never verified as Claude, including with Claude-named toasts or output anywhere in the pane
